title: The dwarf galaxy IC 1613

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This image from ESO's VLT Survey Telescope in Chile shows IC 1613, a small dwarf galaxy in the constellation of Cetus. It was captured with OmegaCAM, the telescope's camera, and what makes this galaxy notable is how clean it is.

Most galaxies are laced with dust, fine grains that absorb and scatter starlight and hide much of what lies behind them. IC 1613 contains very little of this dust. That lack of dust gives astronomers an unusually clear view into the galaxy and everything it contains.

Dwarf galaxies are far smaller and fainter than big spirals like our own Milky Way, but they are common, so an unobscured one is valuable to study. With so little dust in the way, astronomers can explore the contents of IC 1613 without the usual veil dimming and reddening the light from its stars.

understand.summary: This is a visible-light image made with the OmegaCAM camera on ESO's VLT Survey Telescope, using u, g and r filters plus a hydrogen-alpha filter. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: The camera's long exposures gather far more light than the eye, bringing out faint detail in the galaxy.
